commons.title: LencaMarket.jpg
commons.description: Daily Lenca produce market in La Esperanza, Honduras
commons.editorial_reason: Although labeled a Lenca market, the image visibly shows a generic produce stand without distinctive cultural content.

commons.title: Managuara ritual vessel.jpg
commons.description: This is one of the pictographic representations linked to a Lenca religious celebration; in this instance, we see a possible ritual or "dance" dedicated to a serpentine deity—specifically Managuara, known as the Lenca deity with reptilian features
commons.editorial_reason: Caption links the depicted ritual vessel and serpentine deity imagery specifically to a Lenca religious celebration.

commons.title: Icelaca Lenca god of time and the seasons.jpg
commons.description: This is a hypothetical reconstruction based on the few surviving descriptions; there are very few surviving depictions of this deity, but I was able to create this version using those descriptions and certain graphic elements.
commons.editorial_reason: The description identifies this as a hypothetical modern reconstruction/digital artwork, not an authentic cultural depiction.

commons.title: Berta Cáceres (ink drawing).jpg
commons.description: Berta Cáceres, Honduran environmental activist, indigenous leader, and co-founder and coordinator of the Council of Popular and Indigenous Organizations of Honduras (COPINH). Ink portrait.
commons.editorial_reason: This is a portrait of a modern activist; it shows no traditional dress, craft, performance, or other visible cultural content.
